title: Sheet and Drawing Numbering Profiles
resolver_rule: Select the highest-precedence applicable numbering profile. Lower-precedence profiles may supply only unresolved definitions permitted by the higher authority; they shall not silently replace or contradict it.

profiles.name: Governed CDE / Document-Control Numbering
profiles.selection: Use when the project has an authority-, client-, contract-, EIR-, project-information-standard-, or CDE-governed document numbering convention.
requirements: Resolve the governing document-number grammar before first formal registration.
Preserve semantic classification separately from the generated document number.
Treat CDE platform configuration as implementation evidence, not as authority unless the governing project arrangement explicitly makes it authoritative.
Validate project stage, work condition, spatial metadata, discipline, information form, content classification, sequence, status/suitability, revision, and title as required by the selected profile.
After first formal registration or issue, identity changes require governed document-control change rather than casual authoring-tool renumbering.

profiles.name: Qatar / Ashghal Drawing Identity
rules: The drawing identity follows the applicable Ashghal/project requirement; TIVERIT shall not substitute a simplified sheet-number syntax.
Project stage is governed metadata and is not assumed to be an identity field unless the applicable project requirement says so.
The final number/sequence shall follow the applicable Ashghal/project rule; TIVERIT shall not invent content-series meanings where the authority material is silent.
Where implemented in Aconex or another CDE, the authority requirement remains upstream of platform configuration.

profiles.name: Client / Project-Specific Governed Numbering
profiles.selection: Activate only when governing project evidence establishes a project-specific numbering convention. Public TIVERIT examples shall use neutral placeholders such as AAA, WWW, ZZZ, Project A, Zone A, or Client A rather than real client or project identifiers.

confirmed: A large project sheet register can provide strong evidence of a consistently implemented project numbering convention when the pattern is systematic and was used for formal submission.
Project phase and project stage are separate semantic dimensions and shall not be inferred from document status or work condition.
Project zone/sub-zone and discipline structures may supply semantic classification where governing project evidence defines them.

The authoring-tool sheet identity and the submitted information-container identity may differ where an export or document-control process adds information-form or deliverable designations after sheet production.
not_yet_confirmed: Whether an evidenced project convention is an enterprise-wide client standard unless governing client evidence or multiple governed projects establish that applicability.
Whether project phase or project stage is encoded in the document number versus metadata unless the governing project convention explicitly defines it.
Any field order, code, content range, or CDE mapping not supported by curated project evidence.

submission_identity_transform.rule: The submission process may add an information-form or deliverable designation after authoring-tool sheet output. The added designation is part of the governed submission/container identity and shall not be reinterpreted as sheet content classification.
submission_identity_transform.implementation_note: A post-export automation may perform the transformation, but the tool does not create authority and the exact submission filename/document-number grammar must come from project evidence.

rules: Do not publish real confidential or project-specific names, codes, zones, sheet numbers, or identifiers as TIVERIT defaults or examples; substitute neutral placeholders while preserving the tested structure.
Do not generalize a project-specific convention into a national or enterprise client convention without governing evidence.
Treat CDE platform configuration as implementation evidence rather than upstream authority unless the project arrangement explicitly makes it authoritative.

Preserve project phase/stage, work condition, zone/sub-zone, discipline, content class/subtype, status/suitability, revision, title, and information form as separate semantic dimensions until governing evidence maps them into identity fields.

Where a submission workflow adds a deliverable or information-form designation after authoring-tool output, model that as a governed identity transformation rather than changing the semantic sheet classification.
A project-evidenced content-series mapping may resolve sheet classification only when the active project profile explicitly adopts that mapping; it is not a TIVERIT universal default.
If the submission identity grammar remains unresolved, the authoring sheet number may be resolved while the submission pre-registration gate remains unresolved.
Once additional governing evidence is curated, map it to the common semantic classification rather than redefining semantic classes.

profiles.name: Simplified Non-CDE Sheet Numbering
profiles.selection: Use only where no higher-precedence authority, client, project, or governed CDE numbering requirement applies.
rules: Use the common semantic classification registry.
A compact TIVERIT numbering syntax may be selected only after higher-precedence requirements have been checked and found silent or inapplicable.
Legacy D-18/D-19 style discipline/series/sequence concepts may be considered for this fallback profile only after the content taxonomy research is complete; they are not universal defaults.

suspended_decisions.reason: Research established that international, authority, client, project-information-standard, BEP, and CDE requirements must resolve first. A TIVERIT discipline/series/sequence convention may survive only as a lower-precedence simplified fallback profile.
